subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic skill-authored setup execution during install/update, and if so should that live in the core lifecycle or remain an external ClawHub/admin plugin workflow?
rationale: Running third-party skill scripts during install/update changes the host execution and credential-exposure boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Add a guarded core lifecycle hook
options.body: Implement setup metadata plus install/update execution only with explicit user consent, constrained paths, selected environment values, timeouts, logs, redaction, and focused fresh-install/upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep setup manual via plugin
options.body: Treat the published skills-setup ClawHub plugin and SDK helper work as the supported path, and close or narrow this issue to documentation and helper gaps.

options.title: Defer until skill trust model lands
options.body: Pause automatic setup execution until skill permission manifests, install scanners, and broader skill trust UX are decided.

recommendation.title: Add a guarded core lifecycle hook
recommendation.body: Implement setup metadata plus install/update execution only with explicit user consent, constrained paths, selected environment values, timeouts, logs, redaction, and focused fresh-install/upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core skill lifecycle, ClawHub/plugin boundaries, and security posture, and this owner has the strongest maintainer-context signal in the related area history.
